value.verdict: Partially confirmed, not exact. cascade_blocked (1281) matches the claim exactly. causal (128 vs ~127) is within rounding. infra is undercounted by the campaign by exactly 18 — those 18 are a 'frozen manifest validation failed: ...' family that measures as infra-class (guardian-shaped: engine self-protection, not a data/logic bug) but was evidently not folded into the original 543. silent_empty_error is overcounted by the campaign by 6 (307 claimed vs 301 measured) — plausibly measurement-time drift: build_runs/build_run_assets are subject to a live 90-day retention prune (M-4, cockpit/watchdog/route.ts) that runs on every 5-minute watchdog tick, and the oldest failed records in this population sit right at the 90-day boundary (earliest error/aborted record: 2026-06-28, vs today 2026-09-26), so a handful of the oldest empty-error rows the campaign counted may have been pruned since. Also notable: the campaign's own four parts sum to 2258, not to its own stated headline of 2283 — a 25-record internal inconsistency independent of anything measured here.

campaign_claim_reconciliation.population: all build_run_assets rows with state IN ('error','aborted'), classified by error-text prefix family
campaign_claim_reconciliation.query: SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE error ILIKE 'BLOCKED: upstream dependenc%') AS blocked, count(*) FILTER (WHERE error IS NULL OR btrim(error)='') AS empty_error, count(*) FILTER (WHERE error IS NOT NULL AND btrim(error)<>'' AND error NOT ILIKE 'BLOCKED: upstream dependenc%' AND (error ILIKE 'guardian_cleanup%' OR error ILIKE 'orphaned_by_crash%' OR error ILIKE 'manual reap%' OR error ILIKE 'worker_crash%' OR error ILIKE 'frozen manifest validation failed%')) AS infra, count(*) FILTER (WHERE error IS NOT NULL AND btrim(error)<>'' AND error NOT ILIKE 'BLOCKED: upstream dependenc%' AND NOT (error ILIKE 'guardian_cleanup%' OR error ILIKE 'orphaned_by_crash%' OR error ILIKE 'manual reap%' OR error ILIKE 'worker_crash%' OR error ILIKE 'frozen manifest validation failed%')) AS causal_or_other, count(*) AS total FROM build_run_assets WHERE state IN ('error','aborted');

value.verdict: ONE dominant cluster / ONE dominant root cause. 295 of 301 records (98.0%) trace to a single build_runs.last_error message — 'orphan-watchdog: run never dispatched' — written by exactly one code path (the watchdog's undispatched-run reaper). A second, much smaller cluster (3 records, 1 run) traces to a structurally identical but distinct dispatch-failure path (invokeRunJob env-var failure). 2 records are genuinely unattributable even at the run level. This is a single defect class (a missing error-text propagation in the 'abort queued assets on dispatch failure' idiom), but that idiom is copy-pasted across at least 4 call sites, so the FIX is one pattern applied at multiple sites, not one file edit.

cross_reference_build_events_and_noop_ev.population: build_events.build_id and orchestrator_noop_events.run_id matched against the 46 distinct run_ids behind the 301 empty-error records
cross_reference_build_events_and_noop_ev.query: SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT build_id) FROM build_events WHERE build_id IN (SELECT DISTINCT run_id::text FROM build_run_assets WHERE state IN ('error','aborted') AND (error IS NULL OR error ~ '^\s*$')); -- and the equivalent against orchestrator_noop_events.run_id
cross_reference_build_events_and_noop_ev.verdict: CAPTURE FIX is not needed for the dominant cluster — it is a PLUMBING FIX. build_events and orchestrator_noop_events are both emitted by the Python orchestrator process itself, which for every one of these 46 runs never started (that is the entire content of 'run never dispatched') — so there is nothing anywhere else in the engine that knows more than build_runs.last_error already records. The information exists exactly once, at the run level, and simply never gets copied down to the per-asset error column.

This UPDATE can never match a row: it is dead code masquerading as a fix.
